title: Prompting for Humanity: Teaching AI to Ask Better Questions Than It Answers
author: Colette Molteni
summary: Colette Molteni draws on personal workplace stories to argue that in human-AI collaboration the human's skills, especially emotional intelligence and the discipline of asking better questions, matter more than the model. Recounting a data project that hit a major blocker four months in, a coding challenge where she snapped at an in-house LLM before recovering her Stoic center, and a high-stakes presentation she pressure-tested by asking AI to expose her assumptions and biases, she shows how pausing to interrogate one's own thinking turns AI into a genuine partner. She also warns that grand AI-first declarations without context or purpose create organizational risk, and that leaders should ask precise questions to keep teams off dead-end roads. Her throughline: AI can accelerate work only if humans bring the emotional intelligence to slow down, break problems down, and ask sharper questions.
points: Molteni's core claim is that in AI collaboration your skills matter more than the model, with question-asking and emotional intelligence as the decisive human contributions.
She reframes a stalled project and a frustrating LLM session as prompts to interrogate her own assumptions rather than spiral or blame the tool.
She uses AI adversarially, asking it to uncover her assumptions and biases before a senior leader could, to prepare for a high-stakes presentation.
She warns that sweeping AI-first declarations without context or purpose create organizational risk rather than advantage.
Her Stoic framing treats frustration as a signal, not a verdict, an invitation to return to reason before reaction.
quotes: Empathy in moments like this isn’t about being softer. It’s about understanding the perspectives behind the questions you didn’t ask.
But is having AI competitive if you do not know how it is enabling you to compete?
The Stoics would remind us that frustration is a signal, not a verdict, rather an invitation to return to reason before reaction.
AI can accelerate us, but only if we bring the emotional intelligence to slow down, ask sharper questions, and examine our own thinking.
If you do not have questions about how to leverage AI, and to the benefit of your stated objective, you are proclaiming risk.
It was about the courage to pause, question my assumptions, and begin again with intention.
